name: Italian Game
summary: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4: the bishop aims at f7 at once. White develops fast, castles, and builds the centre with c3 and d4, either at once for open lines or slowly after d3.

white: Develop the kingside fast and castle: Nf3, Bc4, O-O.
Prepare d4 with c3. Play it at once for open lines, or after d3 for a slow build-up.
In the slow lines, re-route the queen's knight: Nbd2, Nf1, Ng3, aiming at f5.
Keep the light-squared bishop: retreat it to b3 or c2 before ...Na5 or ...d5 can hit it.
Watch f7: Ng5 and Bxf7+ ideas work only while f7 has few defenders.
black: Hit e4 with ...Nf6 and, when it is safe, strike with ...d5.
Develop the dark-squared bishop to c5 and keep it with ...a6 and ...Ba7.
Answer Ng5 with ...d5 and ...Na5, not with a recapture that leaves f7 bare.
In the slow lines, play ...h6 against Ng5 and Bg5, then ...Re8 and ...Be6 to trade White's best bishop.

structures.name: Giuoco Pianissimo: c3, d3, e4 against d6, e5
structures.text: A closed, slow centre. Neither side can break at once, so the game turns on piece manoeuvres: White's knight journey to g3 and a later d4, Black's ...Be6 to trade bishops and ...d5 when ready.

structures.name: Open centre after c3 and d4
structures.text: When Black takes on d4, White gets pawns on d4 and e4 and quick development. Black must hit that centre at once with ...d5 or with the check ...Bb4+, before e5 or d5 drives the knights back.

white: c4 bishop: the soul of the opening. It points at f7; keep it with Bb3 and Bc2.
f3 knight: guards e5 and d4, and jumps to g5 against f7 when ...h6 has not been played.
Queen's knight: d2, f1, g3 in the slow lines; c3 in the open ones.
e1 rook: supports e4 and a later d4.
black: c5 bishop: aims at f2. Give it a retreat on a7 with ...a6.
f6 knight: attacks e4 and defends h7; it makes ...d5 possible.
Light-squared bishop: e6 to trade White's bishop, or g4 to pin the f3 knight before h3.

lines.name: Giuoco Pianissimo: the slow build-up
lines.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. c3 Nf6 5. d3 d6 6. O-O O-O 7. Re1 a6 8. Bb3 Ba7 9. h3 h6 10. Nbd2 Re8 11. Nf1 Be6

notes.1.e4: Takes the centre and opens lines for the queen and the light-squared bishop.
notes.2.Nf3: Develops with a threat: the knight attacks e5.
notes.2...Nc6: Defends e5 by developing a piece.
notes.3.Bc4: The Italian bishop aims at f7, the square only Black's king defends.
notes.3...Bc5: Black mirrors: the bishop aims at f2.
notes.4.c3: Prepares d4 to take the whole centre, and gives the bishop a retreat on c2.
notes.4...Nf6: Develops with an attack on e4.
notes.5.d3: Defends e4 calmly. White keeps d4 in reserve and plays a long game.
notes.6.O-O: The king is safe and the rook can come to e1.
notes.7.Re1: Supports e4 and frees f1 for the queen's knight.
notes.7...a6: Makes room for the bishop on a7, where b4 and d4 cannot hit it.
notes.8.Bb3: Steps out of reach of ...d5 and ...Na5 before they come with tempo.
notes.9.h3: Stops ...Bg4 pinning the f3 knight, and ...Ng4 jumping at f2.
notes.9...h6: The same idea for Black: no Bg5 pin and no Ng5.
notes.10.Nbd2: The start of the knight's journey: d2, f1, then g3.
notes.11.Nf1: The knight goes to g3 next, eyeing f5 and h5.
notes.11...Be6: Offers to trade White's strongest piece, the bishop on b3.

lines.name: Two Knights with 4.d3: no early fight
lines.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nf6 4. d3 Be7 5. O-O O-O 6. Re1 d6 7. c3 Na5 8. Bb5 a6 9. Ba4 b5 10. Bc2

notes.3...Nf6: The Two Knights Defence: Black attacks e4 at once instead of developing the bishop first.
notes.4.d3: Defends e4 and avoids the sharp lines after 4.Ng5 or 4.d4. White builds with O-O, Re1 and c3.
notes.6.Re1: Supports e4 and prepares the slow plan with c3 and d4.
notes.7.c3: Gives the bishop the c2 square and prepares d4.
notes.7...Na5: Hunts the bishop: White's best attacking piece must not stay on c4.
notes.8.Bb5: The bishop avoids the trade and heads for c2 by a longer road.
notes.9...b5: Black gains queenside space with tempo.
notes.10.Bc2: The bishop is safe on c2 and still aims at the kingside. Black's advanced queenside pawns can become targets for a4 later.

lines.name: 4.Ng5: the knight attack on f7
lines.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nf6 4. Ng5 d5 5. exd5 Na5 6. Bb5+ c6 7. dxc6 bxc6 8. Be2 h6 9. Nf3 e4 10. Ne5 Bd6

notes.4.Ng5: Two pieces hit f7. White moves a piece twice because the threat is concrete.
notes.4...d5: The right defence: block the bishop's diagonal at once.
notes.5.exd5: White takes and keeps the pressure on f7.
notes.5...Na5: Black hits the bishop. The recapture 5...Nxd5 would leave f7 open to Nxf7 or d4.
notes.6.Bb5+: The check keeps the extra pawn.
notes.8.Be2: The bishop goes home. White is a pawn up, but Black leads in development.
notes.9...e4: Gains space and drives the knight away.
notes.10...Bd6: Black develops towards the e5 knight and the white king. Active pieces are Black's payment for the pawn.

lines.name: 4.c3 and 5.d4: the open centre
lines.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. c3 Nf6 5. d4 exd4 6. cxd4 Bb4+ 7. Bd2 Bxd2+ 8. Nbxd2 d5 9. exd5 Nxd5 10. Qb3 Nce7 11. O-O O-O

notes.5.d4: The direct plan: two pawns in the centre at once.
notes.5...exd4: Black must take, or dxe5 hits the f6 knight.
notes.6.cxd4: White now has the ideal pawn centre on d4 and e4.
notes.6...Bb4+: A check that gains time and asks White how to block.
notes.7.Bd2: The safe block: trade bishops and keep the centre.
notes.8...d5: The key counter: Black strikes at the centre before e5 can be played.
notes.9...Nxd5: The knight lands on a strong central square.
notes.10.Qb3: Pressure on d5 and b7: two targets at once.
notes.10...Nce7: Defends the d5 knight a second time.
notes.11...O-O: White has an isolated pawn on d4: space and active pieces now, a weakness later.

traps.name: Légal's mate: the pin that was not a pin
traps.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 d6 4. Nc3 Bg4 5. h3 Bh5 6. Nxe5 Bxd1 7. Bxf7+ Ke7 8. Nd5#

notes.3...d6: Solid but passive: it shuts in the f8 bishop.
notes.4...Bg4: Pins the f3 knight to the queen. A pin against a queen is not absolute: the knight may still move.
notes.6.Nxe5: The knight walks out of the pin and offers the queen.
notes.6...Bxd1: Greed: taking the queen allows mate.

traps.punishment: 7.Bxf7+ Ke7 8.Nd5# is mate: Black's own pieces take the king's squares. After 6.Nxe5 Black had to play 6...Nxe5 and stay a pawn down, not a game down.

traps.name: Blackburne Shilling Gambit: do not take on e5
traps.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nd4 4. Nxe5 Qg5 5. Nxf7 Qxg2 6. Rf1 Qxe4+ 7. Be2 Nf3#

notes.3...Nd4: A cheap trick: the knight leaves e5 undefended on purpose.
notes.4.Nxe5: The mistake: the pawn is poisoned.
notes.5.Nxf7: Greed again: it forks the queen and the rook, but Black's attack comes first.

traps.punishment: 4...Qg5 attacks the e5 knight and g2 at once. After 5.Nxf7 Qxg2 6.Rf1 Qxe4+ 7.Be2 Nf3# Black mates; even the best defence 5.Bxf7+ leaves White worse. Against 3...Nd4 play 4.Nxd4 exd4 5.O-O: the knight on d4 is a loose piece, not a threat.
